speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities, along with low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To better understand your condition, please describe the onset and progression of these symptoms in your own words.

REQUEST TEST: CBC, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Liver Function Tests, and IgM/IgG for Rubella.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_scan_of_rash.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results showing normal CBC and metabolic panels are helpful, but they do not yet explain your rash or the respiratory symptoms. When you developed your fever, headache, and runny nose, was it preceded by contact with anyone who had a similar illness or who was pregnant?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Rubella (German Measles).

The classic progression of a low-grade fever, upper respiratory symptoms, followed by a rash that starts on the face and spreads downward while sparing the perioral area is highly characteristic of rubella. Given the patient's age and the specific nature of the rash, this fits the clinical picture perfectly.
